definitions.explanation: Living, green grass or plants, as opposed to dried or withered vegetation. Evokes the fresh, vibrant greenery of spring and summer.

examples.japanese: {青草|あおくさ}の{匂|にお}いがする。
{牛|うし}が{青草|あおくさ}を{食|た}べている。
examples.english: The cows are eating fresh grass.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}になると{野原|のはら}が{青草|あおくさ}で{覆|おお}われて、{気持|きも}ちのいい{季節|きせつ}だ。
examples.english: In spring the fields are covered with green grass — it's a pleasant season.

notes:
A compound of {青|あお} (green/blue) and {草|くさ} (grass/plants). In Japanese, {青|あお} is traditionally used for the color of vegetation, not {緑|みどり}. This is the same usage seen in {青葉|あおば} (green leaves) and {青田|あおた} (green rice paddies).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {青草|あおくさ}の{匂|にお}い — the smell of fresh grass
- {青草|あおくさ}を{刈|か}る — to mow green grass
- {青草|あおくさ}が{生|は}える — green grass grows

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {雑草|ざっそう} — weeds (unwanted plants, regardless of color)
- {芝生|しばふ} — lawn; turf (cultivated grass)
- {枯|か}れ{草|くさ} — dried/dead grass (the opposite of {青草|あおくさ})
- {牧草|ぼくそう} — pasture grass; fodder (grass specifically for livestock)
